title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 61
paragraphs: When Themistocles spoke thus, the Corinthian Adeimantos attacked him a second time, telling him to be silent because he had no native land, and urging Eurybiades not to put to the vote the proposal of a man who was citizen of no city; he said that Themistocles might bring opinions before the council only if he could point to a city of his own, otherwise not. He made this objection because Athens had been taken and was held by the enemy. At this Themistocles said many harsh things of him and of the Corinthians both, and declared that he and his countrymen did in truth have a city and a land larger than the Corinthians', so long as they had two hundred ships fully manned — for none of the Greeks would be able to repel the Athenians if they came to fight against them.
